record.original_question: Do analytic actions of surface groups on R2 satisfy the Milnor–Wood inequality?

evidence.quote: Question 3.17 (Calegari). Do analytic actions of surface groups on R2 satisfy the Milnor–Wood inequality?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma_g$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g \geq 2$, and let $\pi_1(\Sigma_g)$ denote its fundamental group. Consider real-analytic actions of $\pi_1(\Sigma_g)$ on the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, i.e., homomorphisms $\rho: \pi_1(\Sigma_g) \to \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ into the group of real-analytic diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^2$. To any such action one can associate an Euler number $e(\rho) \in \mathbb{Z}$ (for instance, via the induced action on the circle at infinity or via the pulled-back Euler class on $\Sigma_g$). The classical Milnor–Wood inequality asserts that for flat $\mathrm{Homeo}_+(S^1)$-bundles over $\Sigma_g$ one has $|e(\rho)| \leq |\chi(\Sigma_g)| = 2g-2$.

Question: Does every real-analytic action $\rho: \pi_1(\Sigma_g) \to \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ satisfy the Milnor–Wood inequality
$$|e(\rho)| \leq 2g - 2\,?$$
artifact.category_tag: Surface group actions and Milnor–Wood inequality
artifact.status_search_result: The question, attributed to Calegari, asks whether analytic actions of surface groups on the plane satisfy the Milnor–Wood inequality. Web searches reveal substantial related work on Milnor–Wood inequalities for circle bundles and surface group actions on $S^1$ (Goldman, Burger–Iozzi–Wienhard, Calegari–Walker, Mann, Hamenstädt), but no published resolution of the specific question for analytic actions on $\mathbb{R}^2$. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Milnor–Wood inequality and surface group representations into Homeo+(S^1).
status_evidence.claim: Milnor–Wood inequality is well established for circle actions; analytic plane actions are not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Milnor–Wood inequality - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Classical statement: |e| ≤ |χ(Σ)| for flat circle bundles.
status_evidence.claim: Standard inequality known for circle bundles; the analytic R^2 version is not stated as resolved.
